bib.title: A Survey of Prompt Engineering Methods in Large Language Models for Different NLP Tasks

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "A Survey of Prompt Engineering Methods in Large Language Models for Different NLP Tasks", Shubham Vatsal & Harsh Dubey (NYU), arXiv:2407.12994v2, 24 Jul 2024, preprint (not peer reviewed).

COVERAGE: Roughly 92,500 of 115,368 extracted chars read, which is every page of body text (abstract, sec 1-4, taxonomy, Tables 1-29). Pages 1-30 are the body and conclusion. The remaining pages are the reference list, which I skimmed only for the first entries. I did not check the page count of the PDF. The extraction is usable; letter spacing is slightly broken ("P rompt", "Y ao"). Some table cells (SoTA, LLM columns) are truncated or missing in the extraction. I could not read those cells. They include Tables 9, 11, 13, 18, 20 and 21, and the Table 19 Ruin Names row. Offsets below are char offsets into the extraction.

DOES IT RUN ITS OWN EXPERIMENTS: No. It is a literature survey. It says "we read and present a survey of 44 research papers which talk about 39 different prompting methods on 29 different NLP tasks". Every number is relayed from the original papers. The survey does not re-verify any of them. Its "SoTA" labels are the authors' own judgement of which prompting method won on each dataset in the source papers.

CLAIMS (all relayed from other papers unless noted; ranked by usefulness to a core-techniques note)

- claim: CoT's largest gain over basic prompting was about 39% on math and about 26% on commonsense (Wei et al. 2022).
  number: ~39% math, ~26% commonsense (maximum gaps)
  setup: Relayed. These are maximum differences across datasets and models in the original paper. The survey gives no model or dataset.
  quote: "with the maximum difference between CoT and Basic prompting results being as big as around 39% for Mathematical Problem Solving task and around 26% for Commonsense Reasoning task"
  where: sec 2.2, p.3, offset ~5900

- claim: Self-consistency's average gain over CoT is 11% on math, 3% on commonsense and 6% on multi-hop.
  number: 11%, 3%, 6%
  setup: Relayed (Wang et al. 2022). The text says "on an average".
  quote: "Self-Consistency on an average achieves 11% gain on Mathematical Problem Solving task, 3% gain on Commonsense Reasoning task and 6% gain on Multi-Hop Reasoning task when compared to CoT."
  where: sec 2.3, p.3

- claim: PoT beats CoT by about 12% on average. PAL is reported to beat CoT and basic prompting, with no figure given. Computation is delegated to an interpreter.
  number: ~12%
  setup: Relayed (Chen et al. 2022a). Tasks are math, table math, contextual QA and conversational QA.
  quote: "PoT gets an average performance gain over CoT of around 12% across Mathematical Problem Solving, Table-Based Mathematical Problem Solving, Contextual Question-Answering and Conversational Contextual Question-Answering tasks."
  where: sec 2.7, p.4

- claim: ToT gives large gains on search-style tasks and a small gain in free-response coherence.
  number: 65% better success on math (Game of 24); ~40% on logic; coherence 7.56 vs 6.93
  setup: Relayed (Yao et al. 2024). The survey's Tables 1-2 list GPT-4 only, on Game of 24 and Mini Crosswords.
  quote: "ToT achieves 65% better success rate than CoT on Mathematical Problem Solving task and around 40% better success rate on different Logical Reasoning task datasets. ToT further achieves coherency score of 7.56 where CoT gets only 6.93 on an average on Free Response task."
  where: sec 2.17, p.6

- claim: ReAct is competitive with CoT but not a clear win on QA. It clearly beats RL baselines on task completion. Act (no reasoning) is worse than ReAct.
  number: more than 10% absolute success rate
  setup: Relayed (Yao et al. 2022b); ALFWorld and WebShop, with PaLM-540B and GPT-3 text-davinci-002 per Table 28.
  quote: "For Multi-Hop Reasoning and Truthfulness tasks, ReAct is able perform better than Basic prompting while being competitive with CoT." / "ReAct outperforms reinforcement learning methods with an absolute improvement of more than 10% in success rates"
  where: sec 2.21, p.7

- claim: Plan-and-Solve beats zero-shot CoT by at least 5% on math and commonsense and about 2% on multi-hop.
  number: >=5%, ~2%
  setup: Relayed (Wang et al. 2023); zero-shot setting.
  quote: "PS prompting method improves the accuracy over CoT by at least 5% for almost all the datasets in Mathematical Problem Solving task in zero-shot setting."
  where: sec 2.11, p.4-5

- claim: Selecting complex exemplars helps. Complex CoT gains 5.3% on average and up to 18%.
  number: 5.3% avg, up to 18%
  setup: Relayed (Fu et al. 2022). Complexity means the number of reasoning steps. Datasets are math, commonsense, table math and multi-hop.
  quote: "Complex CoT achieves on an average a gain of 5.3% accuracy and up to 18% accuracy improvement"
  where: sec 2.6, p.3-4

- claim: Auto-CoT matches or beats manual few-shot CoT by clustering queries and generating chains with zero-shot CoT.
  number: none
  setup: Relayed (Zhang et al. 2022).
  quote: "Auto-CoT either outperforms or matches the performance of few-shot CoT across Mathematical Problem Solving, Multi-Hop Reasoning and Commonsense Reasoning task."
  where: sec 2.5

- claim: Contrastive CoT (positive and negative demos) gains ~10% over CoT on math. Contrastive self-consistency gains >15% over plain SC on math. Both gain >10% on multi-hop.
  number: ~10%, >15%, >10%
  setup: Relayed (Chia et al. 2023).
  quote: "Contrastive CoT on an average is able to gain an average of 10% improvement over conventional CoT for Mathematical Problem Solving task across multiple datasets."
  where: sec 2.13

- claim: Few-shot generally helps but has a cost. It needs curated exemplars and can bias the model toward them. This is the survey's own framing.
  number: none
  setup: General statement, no experiment.
  quote: "few-shot variations to have helped improve the performance but this comes at a cost of carefully preparing few-shot data points as the LLM can show unexplained bias towards the curated few-shot datapoints."
  where: sec 2, p.2

- claim: Verification-style prompts cut hallucination. CoVe beats CoT and basic by at least about 10% on QA and free-response tasks. VE gains up to 10% on multi-hop.
  number: >=10%; up to 10%, up to 2%
  setup: Relayed (Dhuliawala 2023; Zhao 2023a). Table 8 lists LLaMA-65B and LLaMA-2-70B-Chat for CoVe.
  quote: "CoVe is able to outperform CoT and Basic prompting by around at least 10% on Context-Free Question-Answering, Contextual Question-Answering and Free Response tasks."
  where: sec 2.27, p.8

- claim: Telling the model to ignore irrelevant context works. Instructed prompting scores 88.2 on truthfulness (GSM-IC) and beats CoT, Least-to-Most, program prompting and SC. Yet Table 14 names Least-to-Most as the SoTA on GSM-IC.
  number: 88.2 normalized micro accuracy
  setup: Relayed (Shi et al. 2023); GSM-IC.
  quote: "Instructed prompting is able to achieve 88.2 normalized micro accuracy for Truthfulness task and is able to surpass all it's counterparts including CoT, Least-To-Most, Program prompting and Self-Consistency."
  where: sec 2.26, p.8. The survey is internally inconsistent here (Table 14).

- claim: Least-to-Most addresses CoT failing on problems harder than the exemplars. Decomposition methods (DecomP) win multi-hop, list reversal and last-letter tasks. DecomP beats CoT and Least-to-Most by 25% exact match on average on commonsense.
  number: 25% exact match avg
  setup: Relayed (Zhou 2022; Khot 2022). Models are text-davinci/code-davinci era per Tables 3-4.
  quote: "DecomP is able to outperform CoT and Least-to-Most on an average by 25% in terms of exact match for Commonsense Reasoning task."
  where: sec 2.34

- claim: Simple CoT or plain basic prompting often remains SoTA on knowledge-heavy medical QA with strong models. Basic was marked best on MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, MMLU and the USMLE sets, over CoT, SC and Ensemble Refinement. It was also best on BioMRC and MASH-QA. CoT was best on SportsUnderstanding, Web of Lies and the stance datasets. Basic and CoT tied on Causal Judgement.
  number: none
  setup: Survey's own SoTA labels from Tables 5, 7, 8 (GPT-4 and medical LLMs). It notes "many cases a particular LLM has not been experimented with a given prompting method", so these labels are not controlled comparisons.
  quote: "Basic" appears in the SoTA column for MedMCQA, MedQA, PubMedQA, MMLU, USMLE (Table 8) and for BioMRC and MASH-QA (Table 7).
  where: Tables 7-8, p.19-21

- claim: Adding fixed term definitions to the prompt did not help and may confuse the model.
  number: none
  setup: Relayed (Vatsal et al. 2024), medical contextual QA, GPT-4.
  quote: "these term definitions do not really help possibly because of their narrow knowledge scope which may be conflicting with the bigger knowledge base of the LLM."
  where: sec 2.38, p.11

- claim: Other relayed numbers.
  number: MathPrompter 78.7% to 92.5%; CoS up to 60.8% spatial QA; SCoT up to 13.79% over CoT on code; Analogical Reasoning +4% over CoT avg; Synthetic prompting up to 15.6% absolute; Fed-SP/DP 10-20% over CoT; LoT max +3.7/16.2/2.5/15.8/10%; Maieutic up to 20%; CoK +3/3/1/1%; Dater >=2% and >=1%; Chain-of-Table ~3% and ~1.5%; ThoT ~0.56 exact match; NER 0.57 F1.
  setup: Relayed. Each is a best-case or average from the original paper, with no setup in the survey beyond the task.
  quote: "MathPrompter is able to improve the performance on a dataset belonging to Mathematical Problem Solving task from 78.7% to 92.5%." / "CoS achieves an improvement of up to 60.8% accuracy for Spatial Question-Answering task." / "SCoT outperforms CoT by up to 13.79% for the Code Generation task."
  where: sec 2.12, 2.9, 2.10

- claim: The survey's mapping of technique to task (Figure 1 taxonomy and Tables 1-29) shows which techniques were tried on which datasets. By its labels, PoT wins GSM8K and SVAMP, ToT wins Game of 24 and crosswords, CoC wins most BIG-Bench-Hard logic sets, MP wins the NLI, paraphrase and classification tasks, and ReAct wins ALFWorld, WebShop and Fever.
  number: none
  setup: Authors' judgement.
  quote: "we have designated that as the SoTA regardless of the exact LLM used for that technique"
  where: sec 3, p.11

TECHNIQUES COVERED (39, mostly one paragraph each): Basic, CoT, Self-Consistency, Ensemble Refinement, Auto-CoT, Complex CoT, PoT, Least-to-Most, Chain-of-Symbol, Structured CoT, Plan-and-Solve, MathPrompter, Contrastive CoT/SC, Federated SP/DP, Analogical Reasoning, Synthetic Prompting, ToT, Logical Thoughts, Maieutic, Verify-and-Edit, ReAct, Active-Prompt, Thread-of-Thought, Implicit RAG, System 2 Attention, Instructed Prompting, CoVe, Chain-of-Knowledge, Chain-of-Code, PAL, Binder, Dater, Chain-of-Table, DecomP, THOR, Metacognitive Prompting, Chain-of-Event, Basic + term definitions, Basic + annotation guideline + error analysis.

LIMITS
- No new experiments, and no cross-paper normalization. The survey itself says the gains are not comparable. Papers use different LLMs, metrics and dataset versions: "in many works, the authors have experimented with different versions of the same dataset, making it difficult for an absolute comparison". It also says "The performance of a prompting method varies based on the LLM used."
- Gains are given as vague "average", "up to" or "at least" figures. Most carry no model name in the text.
- Most tested models are 2022-2023 era (GPT-3, Codex, PaLM-540B, LaMDA, GPT-3.5, some GPT-4). No reasoning models are covered (o1-style or later). Everything has dated for current models.
- The SoTA column names only the technique, not a model or metric, and is subjective.
- A technique often appears with a single paper behind it. Some of the self-authored work (Implicit RAG, term definitions) comes from the authors' own prior papers.
- Some entries have no number at all (ER, PAL, Least-to-Most, S2A, CoC, Binder, THOR, MP).
- The conclusion is only three sentences. There is no cost analysis (tokens, calls, latency) and no failure analysis. The authors give no explicit limitations section.
- Minor internal inconsistency: sec 2.28 says "CoVe surpasses CoT, Self-Consistency, VE" in the Chain-of-Knowledge paragraph. That is a typo for CoK.

BUILDS ON (as printed): Sahoo et al. (2024) (29-paper survey, application-based), Edemacu & Wu (2024) (privacy prompting), Chen et al. (2023) (9-10 methods). Core techniques it cites: Radford et al. (2019) zero-shot, Brown et al. (2020) few-shot, Wei et al. (2022) CoT, Wang et al. (2022) Self-Consistency, Yao et al. (2024) ToT, Yao et al. (2022b) ReAct, Gao et al. (2023) PAL, Chen et al. (2022a) PoT, Zhou et al. (2022) Least-to-Most, Zhang et al. (2022) Auto-CoT, Lewis et al. (2020) RAG. Also Vatsal & Singh (2024) and Vatsal et al. (2024).

CODE: none. The survey has no code or prompt templates.

FIGURES: Only one, Figure 1 (p.12-13), "Taxonomy Diagram of Prompt Engineering Methods Across Different NLP Tasks". It is a task-to-technique-list tree. Extracted as text only; I did not render it. Its text lists each task with the techniques tried. The 29 tables (Tables 1-29) map dataset, techniques, LLMs and SoTA.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Extraction has spacing glitches and some truncated table cells (see COVERAGE). The pypdf run printed fontTools warnings, which are harmless. I did not run the figures script. The survey is a thin, descriptive source. Use it for provenance and the relayed numbers, not as independent evidence, and cite the original papers for each number. Working text is at /tmp/vatsal.txt (extracted from /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/01-prompt-engineering/sources/vatsal-2024-survey-prompt-engineering-methods-large.pdf).

NOTE ON TARGET NOTE: I read only the first 60 lines of notes/03-core-techniques.md. It already cites the originals for CoT, Reflexion, ToT (via arXiv links) and states "chain-of-thought lifted GSM8K from 17.9% to 56.9%". The survey adds no new primary evidence. It sharpens the note by citation (the "no technique wins everywhere, task and model matter" point, via the Basic-wins-medical-QA labels and the ~39%/~26% CoT spread). The user's rule says to add a citation and a references row.
